title: When binary powering is exact in a magma
statement: Let (M, ·) be a magma and x ∈ M, with left powers p_1 = x, p_(k+1) = p_k·x. (1) Left-to-right binary powering (B(1) = x, B(2a) = B(a)·B(a), B(2a+1) = B(2a)·x) returns p_e for every e ≥ 1 iff p_a·p_a = p_(2a) for all a ≥ 1 (SQ); it is correct for all e ≤ E iff SQ holds for a ≤ ⌊E/2⌋, so the first wrong exponent is 2a* for the first failing a*. (2) If the left powers are eventually periodic with preperiod μ and period λ (in particular if |M| = m, with μ + λ ≤ m + 1), SQ holds iff it holds for a ≤ μ + λ − 1 (≤ m); the bound is tight for every m ≥ 2. (3) Right-to-left binary powering (s_0 = x, s_(k+1) = s_k·s_k; r = s_k at the first set bit, then r·s_k, resp. s_k·r) returns p_e for every e iff p_a·p_(2^k) = p_(a+2^k) (CL), resp. p_(2^k)·p_a = p_(a+2^k) (CR), for all k ≥ 0 and 1 ≤ a ≤ 2^k; with eventual periodicity it suffices to check k ≤ ⌈log₂(μ+λ−1)⌉ + λ − 1 and a ≤ min(2^k, μ+λ−1). (4) SQ, CL and CR are pairwise independent (all 8 combinations occur at one element of a magma with at most 3 elements); power-associativity implies all three but is not implied by them. Statements (1) and (3) hold in every magma; (2) needs only eventually periodic left powers.

sources.title: Researches in non-associative algebra
sources.venue: D.Sc. thesis, University of Edinburgh (Edinburgh Research Archive)
sources.note: Listed to document the literature search; not used as evidence. The thesis reprints his papers I-X (1937-1941). Read: contents and introduction, paper I, paper II §§1-3, paper X §§1-3, keyword scan of the whole thesis. Primary and plenary shapes, arithmetic of indices of non-associative powers; no condition for binary powering to return the left power.

sources.title: Power-associative rings
sources.venue: Transactions of the American Mathematical Society
sources.note: Listed to document the literature search; not used as evidence. Introduction and §1 read: with Albert's right powers x^(k+1) = x^k x (the left powers p_k of this note), a ring is power-associative iff x^α x^β = x^(α+β) for all positive α, β (the ring version of the equivalence in Definitions). Power-associativity is the sufficient condition of Remark 1. No condition for binary powering.
